newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian TV journalists disappear in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Russian TV journalists disappear in Chechnya.

text.p: Two Russian television journalists have disappeared in Chechnya, sparking fears for their safety a week before post-war elections in the breakaway region, Russian media said on Tuesday.

Russian Public Television (ORT) said its correspondent Roman Perevezentsev and cameraman Vladislav Tibelius were last heard of on Sunday, when they left the Chechen capital Grozny for Nazran in neighbouring Ingushetia to transmit a report.
Their disappearance follows the murder last month of six foreign Red Cross workers in Chechnya -- widely blamed on unnamed forces seeking to disrupt the poll.

That murder prompted concern for the safety of international observers expected in Chechnya to oversee the January 27 elections, which follow a 21-month conflict between Moscow and rebels seeking to split the region from Russia.
"Russian Public Television appeals to all sensible forces in Chechnya with a call to find and return our correspondents and not let them come to any harm," ORT said during a news bulletin.
"Only then will Russia and the rest of the world be convinced that Chechnya is really on the road towards peace and democracy."
"In any case actions linked to the disappearance of the correspondents sharply reduce the likelihood that the elections in six days' time will be recognised as legitimate," it said.

Interfax news agency quoted Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin's spokesman Viktor Konnov as saying on Tuesday the premier was worried about the journalists' fate and was following the situation closely.
